references.text: The children of Israel wandered in the wilderness for forty years because of their fathers' sin—the same event Moses refers to as a warning
The Lord's anger was kindled against Israel when they refused to enter the land, just as Moses warns can happen again
Moses describes how the fathers acted at Kadesh-Barnea—the background for the expression 'raised up in their fathers' place'
The Lord heard the people's words and became angry—parallel to 'the Lord's burning anger against Israel'
Warns against becoming like the fathers, a rebellious and stubborn generation—the same theme of sinful men rising after their fathers
Jesus says 'fill up your fathers' measure'—the same concept of adding to the sins of the fathers
Paul writes that the Jews fill up the measure of their sins—parallel to increasing the Lord's anger
